raw_response:
I've been working this land for 25 years. I know Quzhou's soil and weather well. My 10.1 mu all goes into the wheat-maize rotation — wheat planted in October after maize harvest, maize seeded in June after wheat harvest. That's what my father did, what my neighbors do, and it's worked for me.

With 7 mouths to feed and some family off working in the city, I need the grain income to stay stable. I can't afford a bad season. So I don't take risks with seed — I buy improved wheat varieties from the township supply station, something like Kenong 199 that handles our winters well. For maize I always go hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the station recommends this year. Hybrid gives me the yield.

For fertilizer, I apply urea and compound fertilizer. I put down more nitrogen than some people say is needed, but I've seen lean harvests when I cut back, and I don't want to gamble. For wheat I split the nitrogen — base application at planting, then topdress at jointing. For maize I do base plus one topdress at big bell stage.

Irrigation is my advantage here. Well water means I control timing. Wheat gets water at sowing, then in winter if it's dry, then at jointing and heading — that's three or four times. Summer maize mostly catches the rain but I'll pump once or twice if July is dry.

I do rotary tillage before wheat seeding every year to incorporate the maize stubble. For maize I just direct seed into the wheat field after harvest — no time to plow properly in June.
